text:
mira: Ok — following the RFC, I'm proposing a phased unbundle 'lattice' approach to break down the runtime monolith into small orthogonal slices. High level: carve narrow feature faces (not full bounded contexts), deploy as lightweight adapters, add a stitch layer that can be removed later. Thinking 3 phases: spike + safety harness, slow-path traffic split, mass cutover.

oliver: Sketch sounds promising. Can you call out what we consider a "narrow feature face" vs a full service?

mira: Narrow feature face = a single, well-contained capability surface (e.g., "prompt validation + canonicalizer" or "kv-prefetch for short sequences"). Should have <2 external downstream dependencies initially and explicit input/output contract. Not a full domain extract.

sam: Two concerns: 1) ownership explosion (we can't end up with 40 tiny services). 2) observability duplication. How does lattice avoid that?

mira: Good call. Ownership: each slice gets temporary stewarding (team A or infra), but we keep a registry and 3-month TTL for responsibility. Observability: we require a shared shim that emits standardized trace + metrics tags. If a slice can't emit, it fails build.

nina: Build failure rule feels strict but useful. For traffic shaping, do you envision canary by request hash, or per-tenant rollout?

mira: Both. Default is hash-based gradual ramp so we avoid tenant fragmentation. Per-tenant only when security/SLAs demand it. We'll support routing policies in the router: {"mode": "hash", "ratio": 0.1} style.

raj: How do we handle KV cache ownership? Lots of slices will want read/write. We need a single source-of-truth or strong fencing to avoid correctness bugs.

mira: Strategy: read-only copies allowed for most slices. Single-writer pattern for mutations — the existing session controller remains canonical during phases. We'll implement optimistic concurrency checks and a small coordination API: /coord/claim for short-lived locks.

oliver: Rollback story? If a slice misbehaves at 50% traffic, do we fail closed to monolith or to a safe fallback?

mira: Fail closed to the monolith. The router will have a fallback map: if slice X responds 5xx or latency>2s for N consecutive requests, route back to canonical producer. We also emit a "slice_fallback" metric.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new feature — added routing fallback alarm to #incidents when slice_fallback > 100/min.

sam: Performance/regression testing: we need a preserved perf harness that runs against slice + monolith combo. Suggest adding a synthetic workload job that hits both paths in CI and compares p95 token latency and tails.

mira: Agreed. I'll draft the CI job. Also propose a 'contract test' suite (small, deterministic prompts) that each slice must pass before traffic ramp.

nina: Security review? Some slices will handle raw prompt data — make sure DLP/KMS access isn't duplicated. Add a checklist item: "does slice escalate scope for secrets?"

mira: Added. Also: rollout cadence — target 1 slice per sprint for first 6 sprints, then ramp if automation holds. Smaller slices in parallel but limited to 3 concurrently.

raj: One more: how do we avoid long-term service sprawl? When do slices get merged or retired?

mira: Lifecycle policy: after 6 months if slice passes stability and ownership, either: 1) folded into owning service, or 2) promoted to standalone with permanent owners. We'll enforce a quarterly audit in the console.

oliver: Sounds practical. Can you summarize next steps with owners?

mira: Next steps: 1) I'll ship the 'steward registry' schema (mira) 2) infra team to add routing fallback alarm (raj + infra) 3) sam to prototype CI perf job (sam) 4) nina to add security checklist item (nina) 5) small spike: implement one slice for "prompt canonicalizer" (mira + oliver). Aim to start spike next Monday.

sam: I'll start on the CI prototype today.

raj: Working on alarm config — will ping infra-bot PR.

nina: Adding checklist to security runbook.

mira: Great — if no objections I'll convert this into a short RFC follow-up doc and a 1-pager runbook. :thumbsup:
